rules.project/purpose-and-compatibility: INDIGO is an astronomy device framework and software bus, with native/legacy protocol adapters, server, tools and modular device drivers. Core code is C, with C++, Objective-C, Python, shell and browser assets where already established. Linux, macOS and Windows support must be preserved. Workflow adoption does not change application behavior or public properties.

rules.project/commands:
All commands start at the Git root unless an explicit -C changes directory. Factory requires Python 3.9+ and Git 2.38 or newer.
- Ticket flow checks: `python3 .factory2/factory.py flow check TICKET_ID` runs the checks configured in `.factory2/config.json`; a passing flow check is not application or hardware certification.
- Native build: `make all`; Windows: `msbuild indigo_windows.sln /t:Build /p:Configuration=Release`. Review scope first: broad native builds can include off-limits drivers and vendor SDKs.
- Native unit suite: `make -C indigo_test test-unit`, requiring a built INDIGO library and the agent_platesolver, agent_scheduler and system_alpaca driver archives. The flow check `unit` runs for changes under indigo_libs/, indigo_server/, indigo_test/unit/, indigo_test/test_runner.h or indigo_test/Makefile; its single command generates Makefile.inc, builds the library and those three archives incrementally from the ticket worktree into its gitignored build/ directory and runs the suite (about 2.5 minutes from a fresh worktree, about 1 minute when built). Full native suite: `make -C indigo_test test`; the opt-in Bash tools in indigo_test/shell_compliance/ are separate from this suite.
- Driver runs require an explicit interactive/non-interactive and simulator/hardware mode, then the final recorded run through `python3 tools/run_driver_test.py <driver>`; preserve per-driver commit units.
- Dependencies remain managed by existing makefiles, vendored SDKs and platform projects. No new package manager, dependency installation or hosted CI is introduced. Tests run through the local Makefile targets; no hosted CI is configured.
rules.project/xcode-metadata-boundary: Xcode projects must not reference .factory2 or any descendant through groups, folder/file references or build membership. Factory ticket and archive changes must not modify project.pbxproj. Application build/source objects and the actual Factory records stay independent.
rules.project/documentation: New project documents are English. Keep current project facts in the project rule files, work records and findings in Factory tickets, and durable Factory decisions under indigo_docs/decisions/. Product/developer documentation remains under indigo_docs/. This project has no docs/ directory: indigo_docs/ takes its place everywhere, including Factory paths that mention docs/.
